lang.name: English
app.title: Network Map
tip.listening: Listening to all broadcast and multicast traffic: DHCP hostnames, mDNS, SSDP, LLMNR and NetBIOS.
tip.passiveOff: Start monitoring to listen in. This requires administrator rights.
tip.npcap: Npcap present: ARP frames and LLDP are visible too.
tip.noL2: Without Npcap only ARP and LLDP are missing; those sit below the IP layer.
empty.title: Nothing mapped yet
empty.body: Press Scan now for a single pass, or Start monitoring to keep following devices as they come and go.
map.caveat: Every host hangs off the gateway. Unmanaged switches and mesh satellites in bridge mode play no visible part in the traffic, so they are not drawn as intermediate hops.
col.name: Name
panel.empty: Pick a device on the map or in the table.
panel.hintModel: "{model}" is a model identifier from the TLS certificate, not a name — identical devices share it.
panel.hintNoName: This device answers no name query at all.
panel.hintTail: Your router may well know it: many devices state their name once in the DHCP request and stay silent afterwards. Check your router's client list, or set one here — it is stored against the MAC address and survives a new IP.
panel.noPorts: No open ports found in the scanned range.
panel.noNames: No source gave up a name.
sec.names: Name — and where it came from
log.title: Log
note.arpConflict: Claims {ip}, which previously belonged to {prev}. This is the pattern of ARP spoofing — or an IP conflict.
err.noGateway: No adapter with a default gateway found — is this machine on a network?
err.notStarted: The app has not started up yet.
err.rawSocket: Passive listening requires administrator rights. Start the app as administrator.
ports.title: Open ports on this machine
ports.summary: {n} open ports · {net} to your whole network · {local} local only
ports.noName: The process behind {n} rows could not be determined. Those are system processes; start the app as administrator to see them.
dns.title: Where is your network talking to?
dns.intro: Set the DNS server in your router to {addr}. From then on every name lookup from every device passes through here, showing you where they talk to — without packet capture.
dns.waiting: No queries received yet. Is the DNS server in your router already set to this address?
ev.dnsNew: {name} looked up {domain} — new for this device
watch.title: What changed?
watch.intro: The app remembers what your network normally looks like and reports only what deviates. The first round sets the norm — after that, everything shown here is new.
watch.none: Nothing has changed since last time.
watch.empty: No baseline yet. Scan your network, then record it.
watch.hint: A new device is usually a visitor's phone, and a new port usually something you started yourself. This list does not say anything is wrong — only that it differs from yesterday.
bev.newPort: {name} has port {port} ({service}) open that was not there before
bev.newDomain: {name} looked up {domain} — not seen from this device before
bev.nameChanged: Device with MAC {mac} is now called {new}, was {old}
bev.gone: {name} has not been seen for {days} days
